references.text: The preceding verse specifies the value for a man between 20 and 60 years old as 50 shekels, while this verse sets the value for a woman in the same age group at 30 shekels.
Continuation of the valuation system that assigns different values based on age and gender.
Another section of the Mosaic Law that distinguishes between male and female children in the context of purification periods.
Mentions a redemption price of five shekels of silver, illustrating another example of valuation in shekels within the Mosaic Law.
Refers to 30 shekels of silver as compensation for a slave, the same amount as the value assigned to a woman in Leviticus 27:4.
References the 30 shekels of silver at which the prophet was valued, linking it to the value mentioned in Leviticus 27:4.
Judas receives 30 pieces of silver for betraying Jesus, an amount that can be connected to the valuation of 30 shekels in the Old Testament.
Matthew quotes the prophet regarding the 30 pieces of silver, which relates to the valuation found in Leviticus 27:4.
